builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: CoPyro: Feeding Copy Proposals to Parallel Drafters
summary: CoPyro replaces the mask tokens in parallel speculative drafters (e.g., DFlash) with n-gram copy proposals retrieved from earlier context, letting the drafter keep or revise them in its normal forward pass. Costs include training or fine-tuning the drafter (100K-710K samples), maintaining the retrieval/proposal pipeline, and about 0.24 ms added per decoding round on Qwen3-8B in Transformers. Gains can shrink toward ~1% at larger training scales or different temperatures, benefits are concentrated in repetitive domains such as code, and low-overlap contexts yield few useful copy proposals, so acceptance-length gains may not materialize on the target workload.
rationale: The gain is a modest single-digit improvement in acceptance length that presupposes an existing parallel-drafter speculative decoding stack and drafter training, so it merits validation on the reader's workload before production adoption.
technique: Copy-proposal conditioning for parallel speculative drafters

claims.statement: CoPyro replaces the mask tokens in parallel speculative drafters (e.g., DFlash) with n-gram copy proposals retrieved from earlier context, letting the drafter keep or revise them in its normal forward pass. Costs include training or fine-tuning the drafter (100K-710K samples), maintaining the retrieval/proposal pipeline, and about 0.24 ms added per decoding round on Qwen3-8B in Transformers. Gains can shrink toward ~1% at larger training scales or different temperatures, benefits are concentrated in repetitive domains such as code, and low-overlap contexts yield few useful copy proposals, so acceptance-length gains may not materialize on the target workload.

On Qwen3-4B across eight benchmarks, CoPyro improves overall acceptance length by 2.19-5.08% for four parallel drafters trained on 100K samples; with DFlash trained on 710K samples, gains are 1.08-2.00% across model sizes and temperatures, strongest for code generation.
